description: Unity UI Toolkit support boundary. Ordered; first match wins. Rules classify pointer families for the shapes the dispatcher admits (boolean form controls, select/toggle-item item groups, click-opened non-blocking anchored surfaces); whether a component is admitted at all is the dispatcher's decision, recorded per component in the capability inventory. `lowered` names what the emitter or shared C# runtime performs today; `pending` names the parity phase that will lower the family; `refused` states why UI Toolkit cannot realise the family idiomatically. Catch-all rules exist so that unknown prop families are never silently supported: an allowlisted component that reaches one fails generation until the family is adjudicated here.

phases.P2: Generic anatomy walker: ir.dom/ir.parts lower to a VisualElement tree; runtime bases become behaviors the generated constructor attaches.
phases.P3: Styling projection: generated USS from token facts, variants, states and box-model geometry; hand-authored palette removed.
phases.P4: Interaction families: static pressables, blocking and hover surfaces, composite and non-boolean form controls, componentRef composition, messages, motion, typed C# declarations.
phases.P5: Corpus and admission: allowlist reaches the SwiftUI set; CI compile lane and committed-byte drift diff.

rules.reason: Authoring and validator metadata consumed by the contract validator; no target lowers it into runtime source.

rules.via: C# partial class name and the root USS class added in the generated constructor.

rules.reason: Documentation and classification metadata consumed by docs and audits; no target emits it into component source.
Agent-authoring metadata consumed by the a2ui runtime deriver, outside every emitter.
UI Toolkit panels are retained-mode and are never server-rendered or hydrated.
Icon flipping and row reversal are expressible as generated USS (flex-direction, scale) once styling projection exists; nothing honours rtl today.
The box-model geometry profile projects into generated USS slot defaults.

rules.via: walker.ts (R2, R9): every declared part renders with part identity, name = <part>, the root class carrying cssPrefix and every other part <cssPrefix>__<part>; a parts-only contract synthesizes the tree from ir.parts in declared order.

rules.reason: Prose describing parts; documentation only.
Per-part ARIA roles and attributes have no runtime consumer: UI Toolkit exposes no assistive-technology tree.

rules.via: walker.ts (R1-R3): trigger parts and button tags lower to Button, text-leaf tags carrying content to Label, every other tag to VisualElement; the children tag and an unnamed slot are the contentContainer insertion point, a named slot a public <Name>Slot host.
walker.ts (R1, R4): each ir.compoundParts entry is its own [UxmlElement] <Name><Part> class the consumer composes; a part that opts out stays inline in its parent class.

walker.ts: the part renders with identity (R2); the root role is the generated class, and trigger and content roles are realised through the formControl, interaction and surface facts the IR validates against them (R1, R7).

rules.reason: Overlay parts belong to blocking surfaces and context parts are non-rendered providers; both arrive with the P4 blocking-surface and composition families.

Per-part focusability, interactivity and repetition are realised only where an attached behavior owns the part (trigger Buttons, item-group discovery of repeated compound parts); the walker sets no per-part focus or repetition itself.

A collapse intent replaces the anatomy with a native platform primitive; UI Toolkit's Toggle and Foldout own fixed internal trees the contract's anatomy does not describe, so the walker realises the declared anatomy instead.

rules.via: walker.ts (R5): a componentRef node renders as a placeholder VisualElement carrying part identity and nothing else.

rules.reason: By-reference composition is not lowered: the referenced component, its attrs, bindings and events are not realised; the walker emits an identity-only placeholder.

rules.via: walker.ts (R2): each part node inside a class is a public read-only element property named for the part, added to its parent in document order; an empty attribute or binding map declares nothing to lower.
walker.ts (R3): a named slot lowers to a public VisualElement <Name>Slot host at its position, named for the slot with class <cssPrefix>__<slot>.

rules.reason: Static roles, ARIA attributes, element types and tab indices have no UI Toolkit consumer: there is no accessibility tree, the native Button owns activation, and focus order follows the element tree.
Other static attributes (SVG presentation, text-input hints, data attributes) are not lowered; an allowlisted component that declares one must be adjudicated here.

rules.via: The attached behavior's state class (R7): a binding to the selected channel's value on a trigger part is realised by BooleanControl, ItemGroup or AnchoredSurface toggling is-<value> on the host and, for item groups, on the paired parts. A binding to another channel or on a non-trigger part is unrealised and refuses generation.

walker.ts (R6): a disabled=prop:

binding on the form-control part names the prop emitted as the root's [UxmlAttribute] Disabled, mapped to SetEnabled.

rules.reason: Form serialization attributes (name, value) have no UI Toolkit counterpart: there is no form element to submit.
Dynamic roles and ARIA attributes have no runtime consumer: UI Toolkit exposes no assistive-technology tree.
Other attribute and DOM-property bindings need typed C# props; an allowlisted component that declares one must be adjudicated here.
Authored DOM event handlers need P4 callback declarations. The form-control change event and trigger activation are synthesized by the IR and realised by the attached behavior, not authored here.

Prop, message, projection and transform content needs typed C# props and the message catalog; the walker renders the element (a Label for text leaves) without text. Only literal content lowers (Label.text / Button.text, R5).

Prop and slot presence guards are not lowered: the walker refuses a guarded node (UNITY_UNSUPPORTED_ANATOMY) rather than render it unconditionally. The presence guard the IR synthesizes on an unmount content part is realised by the attached behavior.
Repeated rendering is not lowered; the walker refuses an iterated node (UNITY_UNSUPPORTED_ANATOMY).
Prop-driven CSS custom properties need generated USS variables and typed props; the walker emits nothing for them.
Icon-catalog glyph rendering is not lowered; the icon node renders as an identity-only VisualElement.

rules.via: walker.ts (R2, R3): slot anchors are the walker's part identity (UQuery by name or <cssPrefix>__<part> class replaces the DOM data-slot selector) and named-slot hosts; required is a composition obligation the usage audit checks, not a runtime fact.
[UxmlAttribute] value property (Checked, Open, Value with Values) on the generated root, delegating to the attached behavior; SetValueWithoutNotify silently updates boolean channels.
Imperative initial assignment: a value assigned before panel attachment is the uncontrolled initial state; no separate default property is emitted.
RegisterValueChangedCallback for boolean channels and the ValueChanged C# event for selection channels; Controlled + ValueRequested realise the owner-controlled half of the trio.

rules.reason: HTML form submission fields (name, value) have no UI Toolkit counterpart: there is no form element to serialise into.

rules.via: [UxmlAttribute] Disabled mapped to SetEnabled on the control root; disabled activation leaves state unchanged.

walker.ts item-group vocabulary (R6): [UxmlAttribute] Type, Orientation and ActivationMode (validated against their variant axes) and Collapsible, Loop and UnmountInactive on the generated root drive the attached ItemGroup's SelectionType, Orientation, ActivationMode, Collapsible, Loop and UnmountInactive; emitted only when the contract declares the prop and ItemGroup is attached, initialised from the declared default.

walker.ts item-group vocabulary (R6): [UxmlAttribute] Appearance validated against its variant axis toggles the root's class-recipe modifier (<cssPrefix>--<value>), which the shipped stylesheet keys; P3 moves that styling into generated USS.

[UxmlAttribute] CloseOnEscape / CloseOnOutsideClick / CloseOnBlur on the generated root drive the attached AnchoredSurface's CloseOn<Event> knobs, initialised from the trigger's defaultEnabled; only modes the surface declares start enabled.
[UxmlAttribute] Placement on the generated root, validated against its variant axis, drives the attached AnchoredSurface; floating content flips and shifts at panel edges.

rules.reason: Only the default (md) geometry is lowered from typed token facts; other sizes arrive with USS projection.
DOM id generation exists to wire ARIA relationships; UI Toolkit has no id-referenced accessibility relationships.
DOM attribute passthrough; UI Toolkit controls expose typed properties, not arbitrary host attributes.
Prop families not yet adjudicated for UI Toolkit. An allowlisted component may not rely on this rule: add a family rule above.

rules.via: The one channel the dispatcher selects maps its value/default/change trio to the C# value property, pre-attachment assignment and change callback or event; Controlled + ValueRequested carry owner-controlled state. A second channel is unrealised and refuses generation.

rules.reason: Named types lower to C# string/bool today; enums, unions and records need typed C# declarations.
Variant axes project into generated USS modifier classes; no variant styling is generated today.
Only the behavior's is-<value> state class is derived (from the channel-effect or selection dimension, R7); generic state dimensions and their styling arrive with USS projection.
USS has no @keyframes; it supports property transitions only. Keyframe animation would need a scheduler-driven C# runtime, which is not an idiomatic lowering of a stylesheet fact.
USS transitions, loops and reduced-motion gating are not generated yet.

rules.via: Events emitted through the selected channel's change prop surface as RegisterValueChangedCallback (boolean) or the ValueChanged C# event (selection); C# signatures use arrays for both selection modes. Any other event is unrealised and refuses generation.

rules.reason: Transitions are implemented by hand in ItemGroup and AnchoredSurface; there is no generic state-machine lowering.
No HTML form participation, constraint validation or field association exists in UI Toolkit.

rules.via: The dispatcher attaches the BooleanControl behavior for boolean value models (R7).
The form-control part renders as the Button BooleanControl.Attach binds (exposed as Trigger); the channel selects the generated C# value property and constants.
BooleanControl commits on trigger activation, which is the change moment of a boolean control; there is no intermediate input phase to defer.

rules.reason: Non-boolean value models and commit policies need their own runtime behavior and an explicit decision here.
Composite controls (Select, RadioGroup, …) need a composite runtime behavior; the dispatcher rejects them today.

rules.via: The dispatcher attaches ItemGroup for select / toggle-item and AnchoredSurface for toggle; ItemGroup.Attach(…, operation, …) carries the operation into the runtime.

The trigger and content parts are generated keyed sub-elements (R4) the attached behavior discovers under the host by <cssPrefix>__<part> class; the channel selects the generated value property and constants.
The named prop is emitted as [UxmlAttribute] Disabled and gates activation through SetEnabled.

The dispatcher admits hidden only on ItemGroup (inactive content hidden, detached when UnmountInactive is set) and unmount only on AnchoredSurface (floating content removed on close); other pairings are refused.

rules.reason: Other operations (open, close, …), multi-trigger interactions and remaining interaction facts have no runtime behavior and need an explicit decision here.

rules.via: ItemGroup.Attach(…, orientation, wrap) initialises arrow-key orientation and wrapping; declared orientation / loop props override them through the item-group vocabulary.

The dispatcher pairs each strategy with the behavior that realises it and refuses other pairings (UNITY_UNSUPPORTED_FOCUS): roving and manual on ItemGroup (passed to Attach; arrow / Home / End navigation), auto on BooleanControl (native Button focus), none on AnchoredSurface (no trap; focus stays on the trigger or moves into the content).

rules.reason: The initial focus target is not read. ItemGroup's roving tabIndex makes the active tab, or every trigger, the first tab stop regardless of the declared part; a declared target that differs would be ignored.
Prose description of the focus strategy; documentation only.
Focus trapping, restoration and other focus facts are not lowered and need an explicit decision here.

rules.via: AnchoredSurface reparents floating content to the panel root and re-attaches the stylesheet; the dispatcher refuses any non-surface shape that enables a portal (UNITY_UNSUPPORTED_PORTAL).
Content stays in the document tree; the dispatcher refuses an anchored surface whose portal is disabled because AnchoredSurface always reparents (UNITY_UNSUPPORTED_SURFACE).
The panel root is the UI Toolkit equivalent of document.body.
AnchoredSurface.Reposition anchors to the trigger's world bound and flips/shifts at panel edges.

rules.reason: Floating content is only brought to the front of the panel root; named layers need a generated z-order policy.
Other portal targets, positioning or collision policies need an explicit decision here.

rules.via: AnchoredSurface CloseOnEscape / CloseOnOutsideClick / CloseOnBlur over the anchor/content union.
The named prop is emitted as the matching [UxmlAttribute] CloseOn* flag.
An empty trigger list declares no dismissal; the attached behaviors register none.

rules.reason: pointer-leave, close-button and other dismissal triggers need the blocking and hover surface behaviors and an explicit decision here.

rules.via: The dispatcher attaches AnchoredSurface for non-blocking surfaces.
The trigger Button's clicked event toggles the surface.
The anchor and content parts are generated sub-elements (R1, R4) AnchoredSurface.Attach discovers under the host by <cssPrefix>__<part> class.

Interactive surface content is a generated ScrollView sub-element (R1) the behavior makes focusable; the dispatcher refuses non-interactive content because the runtime cannot make it inert (UNITY_UNSUPPORTED_SURFACE).

rules.reason: aria-controls / aria-expanded relations have no assistive-technology consumer in UI Toolkit.

rules.via: The dispatcher admits part-anchored popovers only; AnchoredSurface.Reposition anchors to the trigger and flips/shifts at panel edges.
The named prop is emitted as [UxmlAttribute] Placement and drives Reposition.
The Content object is retained while closed (detached from the hierarchy, not disposed); the dispatcher refuses other presence values (UNITY_UNSUPPORTED_SURFACE).

rules.reason: Blocking modality, hover/focus open triggers and remaining surface facts need the blocking and hover surface behaviors and an explicit decision here.
Id-referenced ARIA relationships; UI Toolkit exposes no assistive-technology tree that could consume them.

rules.via: ItemGroup arrow / Home / End navigation and native Button submit activation (Space / Enter) through NavigationSubmitEvent.

rules.reason: Roles, labels and ARIA attributes have no runtime consumer: UI Toolkit exposes no assistive-technology tree on desktop, and Unity's mobile AccessibilityHierarchy is not populated by UI Toolkit. Revisit when that integration exists.
The component message catalog is not lowered for Unity; generated controls carry no localisable text.
Truncation policy needs USS text-overflow projection and a measuring runtime.
Sequence and paged-set position policies need their own runtime behavior.

rules.via: walker.ts (R10): typed px fallback facts <prefix>.<axis>.<default>.<part>.<width|height|size> for a variant axis at its declared default set the rendered part's inline style.width / style.height in the generated constructor (size sets both). The pattern names md because the boundary cannot read a default; the walker applies the declared one.

rules.reason: Token bindings project into generated USS variables; today only the default-size geometry fallbacks are read.
Style declarations project into generated USS; the shipped stylesheet is hand-authored.
